identity.name: Indian Creek Village
identity.notes: Exclusive, privately gated island community (~250 acres) in the Indian River Lagoon, accessible only from Surfside via a single community-controlled drawbridge off Indian Creek Drive. One of the wealthiest enclaves in the US, with waterfront mansions, a private marina, and a long history (developed from the 1920s-30s).

fees.note: Indian Creek Community Association assessments commonly cited in the ~$3,000-$6,000+ per year range (varies by lot/property); funds maintenance of the drawbridge, docks, roads, security and common areas. Exact current rate not officially published in readily available sources. No standard CDD assessment known — the community predates CDDs, and periodic special assessments/bonds (e.g., for bridge or seawall work) have historically been levied on top of base dues.
Occasional special assessments / community bonds for major infrastructure repairs (bridge, seawalls, docks) have been levied on lot owners; amounts vary and are not fixed.

amenities.detail: Indian Creek Yacht Club — private lagoon-front marina with private berths/slips for residents' boats and yachts; one of the key draws of the island.
Indian Creek Community Club — private clubhouse for social and club events.
Community swimming pool at the club.
Tennis courts on the island.
Walking/biking paths along the lagoon waterfront and island roads.
Single point of entry: the community-controlled drawbridge on Indian Creek Drive (Surfside) with intercom/resident screening; no public road access to the island.
No golf course on the island itself; nearest major courses include PGA National (Palm Beach, ~30 mi) and Doral Golf Resort's Blue Monster (~25 mi).
Pets generally permitted by the community association; no widely published breed/size restrictions found — confirm with the association before purchase.
Indian Creek Country Club golf course located at the center of the island; residential estates face Biscayne Bay, the Intracoastal Waterway, or the golf course greens
The island is connected to the mainland by only one guarded bridge, with an environment designed around privacy and limited access
Only a few dozen expansive waterfront estates on oversized lots with landscaped grounds and views across Biscayne Bay; no commercial streets or apartment buildings

Indian Creek Country Club – a private golf course located at the center of the island, occupying a large portion of the ~300-acre land area. Estates are arranged in a ring around the course, facing Biscayne Bay, the Intracoastal Waterway, or the golf course greens.
Community lifestyle is described as anchored by a private country club.
Indian Creek Village runs its own police and public safety department with 24/7 coverage and specialized capabilities, including a vehicle screening checkpoint at the island's single bridge.
Associated with an Israeli-designed perimeter security system incorporating radar and thermal/infrared camera surveillance to monitor approaches.
Water approaches are monitored; security posture includes marine patrol and boat monitoring to deter waterborne approaches.

demographics.geography_level: Unincorporated island neighborhood (census block group), Surfside area, Miami-Dade County — not a formal CDP, so ACS figures are small-sample estimates with wide error margins. Community is overwhelmingly owner-occupied and among the highest-income areas in the country (median household income often cited well above $500K, with many multi-million-dollar estates). Median age skews to the late 50s (large retiree/empty-nest population). Owner-occupancy ~90%+. Population estimates vary from ~600 to ~900 depending on source/seasonal residents. All figures are approximate AI-knowledge estimates, not official Census publishes for the island as a named area.
